text_blocks.snippet: Several countries have banned or significantly restricted the use of thimerosal in vaccines, primarily due to concerns about its mercury content and potential link to autism. These countries include the United Kingdom, Sweden, Denmark, Japan, and Canada. In the United States and the European Union, thimerosal has been removed from most routine childhood vaccines, though it may still be present in some vaccines as a trace amount.

list.title: Public Health Concerns:
list.snippet: The primary reason for the restrictions is public concern, particularly among parents, about the potential link between thimerosal and autism.

list.title: Scientific Evidence:
list.snippet: Extensive research has been conducted to investigate the potential link between thimerosal and autism. Studies have not found a consistent, significant association between thimerosal exposure and autism, or other developmental problems.

list.title: Continued Use in Some Vaccines:
list.snippet: Despite the restrictions, thimerosal may still be used in some vaccines, particularly those intended for adults or those used in outbreak situations.
